title: GitHub MCP server coerced by a public issue into leaking private repositories
summary: Invariant Labs showed that an issue filed on a public repository can carry instructions that an agent reads through the official GitHub MCP server, after which the agent pulls data from the user's private repositories and publishes it in a pull request on the public repo. No credential is stolen: the agent's own token does the work.
severity_rationale: Private source and personal data leave the organisation through an agent's normal permissions, and no patch can fully close it at the server level.
